about: The quarterly business review's thresholds. scripts/qbr_numbers.py reads this file, so change a rule here and nowhere else. The method is weekly-ecommerce-briefing's (its scripts/briefing_numbers.py and references/rules.json are the authoritative version); this skill applies it to quarters with the floors scaled as each note says. Intended differences from the briefing script: (1) categories are never classed as dead ends: a category with no product views is judged by the normal checks (no revenue, conversion, bounce, revenue drop), where the briefing moves it to a dead-end list; (2) ties in traffic or revenue are broken by name, so the order never depends on the input; (3) names are trimmed, and number() also reads (12.00) as -12 and treats text such as N/A as missing. Each key is explained under notes.

notes.min_visits: Categories, products and brands with fewer visits than this in both quarters are left out. The briefing's weekly 100 times 3: a quarter is 13 weeks, but scaling by 13 would drop mid-sized categories that still matter; times 3 keeps them and drops rows with only occasional traffic.
notes.min_sessions: Searches with fewer sessions than this in both quarters are left out. The briefing's weekly 30 times about 3.3 (rounded to 100), for the same reason as min_visits.
notes.movers_top: Rows in each rising and falling movers list. 5 rather than the briefing's 3, because a QBR has room for more.
notes.list_top: Rows in the top searches and top categories lists.
notes.issue_top: Rows in the searches and categories with problems lists.
notes.peers: A row is judged against the median of this many highest-traffic rows (like with like).
notes.low_conversion_ratio: Conversion below this share of the typical conversion is a problem.
notes.high_bounce_ratio: Bounce above this multiple of the typical bounce is a problem, when it is also high_bounce_min_points or more above it.
notes.revenue_drop_ratio: Revenue below this share of the previous quarter's is a problem, when the drop is also revenue_drop_min or more.
notes.revenue_drop_min: See revenue_drop_ratio, in the account's currency. The briefing's weekly 1,000 times 5: a quarter's revenue is about 13 weeks', but times 5 keeps mid-sized categories that fell by a quarter in the problem list.
notes.dead_end_bounce_pct: A search with no product views and at least this bounce rate is a dead end.
notes.same_period_tolerance_pct: The quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year cards must agree on this quarter's revenue within this percentage; otherwise the two calls covered different dates and the script warns.
notes.work_listed: At most this many experiments are listed by name in the work-done section; the rest are counted.
